sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: A reporter should write with clarity, ______ and ______ to make a story newsworthy.
Fill in the blanks: ______ and ______ are sources through which a reporter gathers news.
Fill in the blanks: ______ and ______ are the tools required by a sub-editor.
State true or false: (a) The Chief Editor takes care of overall supervision in a newspaper. (b) The reporter's job is to write the story as quickly as possible with all the facts and figures.
Fill in the blanks: Preparing the page of the newspaper is called ______. Earlier sub-editors did it on ______ pages.
Which of the given pairs are attributes of an effective journalist: clarity and sincerity, or friendly and lazy?
Fill in the blanks: A news story's most important opening sentence is the ______; it can be ______ or soft.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is meant by interpretative reporting?
questions.answer: Reporting that analyses news developments, usually done by senior journalists, mostly on political developments.

questions.q: What is meant by 'lead' of a news story?
questions.answer: The opening sentence, the most important part, which attracts the reader's attention.

questions.q: What is a scoop?
questions.answer: An exclusive news report covered by only one reporter, considered a great achievement.

questions.q: What is meant by investigative reporting?
questions.answer: In-depth reporting of a scandal or controversy in all its details, sometimes through a sting operation.

questions.q: Define reporting and editing.
questions.answer: Reporting is gathering facts for a news story; editing is correcting, polishing, condensing and preparing it for publication.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Briefly discuss any three basic facts about reporting with examples.
questions.answer: Finding the lead (opening sentence, e.g. 'PM dies in plane crash'); finding the angle (the most vital part, e.g. farmers' debt relief in the budget); body of the story in inverted pyramid style with important facts first.

questions.q: Which types of news should be refrained from reporting under the ethics of reporting?
questions.answer: Misleading, inaccurate, defamatory, vulgar or obscene news, anything intruding on privacy, and news that harms national interest.

questions.q: Explain the job of a sub-editor in editing a copy.
questions.answer: Correct language and facts, add background, write a crisp heading, add photographs or graphs, condense to fit space and suggest a byline.

questions.q: List the qualities of a good news story.
questions.answer: Clarity, focus, objectivity and credibility with cross-checked facts.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is meant by the 'inverted pyramid' method of writing? Explain in detail.
questions.answer: The most important facts come in the opening paragraphs; importance narrows down to the end; the least important details come last and can be cut without harming the story; it keeps the reader's interest and suits the lead.

questions.q: Describe the sources from which reporters get news.
questions.answer: Listening, covering events, press conferences, reports and statements, Parliament and Assemblies, police sources and interviews.
